close_reason: Fixed in rm8.12: variant removed entirely
description:
src/lib.rs line 343-347 + module rustdoc lines 65-72: IdentityError::NotYetImplemented is retained 'as a non-removed variant so future scaffold-then-fill workflows can reuse it without a breaking API change.'

This is a self-inflicted forever-cost. Once shipped (in 0.1.0, already shipped):

* Every caller's exhaustive-but-future-compatible match must include a NotYetImplemented arm.
* The variant's *Display* string is locked: 'pkix-identity functionality not yet implemented'.
* New developers reading the source will ask 'what's still not implemented?' — the answer is 'nothing, but we keep the variant'. This is confusing onboarding cost.
* Audit / compliance reviewers seeing 'NotYetImplemented' in an enum from a 1.0 crypto-adjacent crate raise eyebrows.

The justification — 'so future scaffold-then-fill workflows can reuse it without a breaking API change' — assumes:

a) The crate will scaffold-then-fill again post-1.0. This is the wrong assumption for a published API. Post-1.0 features are either ready to ship or aren't shipped.

b) Adding a new variant later is a breaking change. Per #[non_exhaustive] on the enum, it is NOT — that's the whole point of #[non_exhaustive] for forward compatibility. So the stated rationale is just wrong.

c) Retaining a dead variant is cheaper than adding one. Backwards: the dead variant pollutes the API in the meantime; the future variant when actually needed would have a meaningful name and meaningful Display message.

PKIX-68mt.2 already flagged that the rustdoc on this variant misstates the current state. That's a doc fix. The deeper fix is: the variant should be removed before 1.0 (which IS a breaking change at 0.2 — acceptable per AGENTS.md prelaunch framing).

Recommend:

1. Document a clear deprecation: mark the variant #[deprecated(since = '0.2.0', note = '...')] in the 0.2 release.
2. Remove it in 0.3 / 1.0.

The rationale in the module docstring ('retained as a non-removed variant so future scaffold-then-fill workflows can reuse it') should be deleted; the #[non_exhaustive] attribute on IdentityError makes the stated benefit moot.

Severity P2: pre-launch is exactly when this should be cleaned up. Punting to post-1.0 is the wrong call per the prelaunch framing in AGENTS.md ('Breaking changes are free. Pre-1.0, semver explicitly permits breaking changes across 0.x releases. They are the *mechanism* for getting the design right.').
title: IdentityError::NotYetImplemented variant is permanent technical debt if 1.0 ships with it
